dimensions.detail: The skill’s core purpose is coherent: fetch or accept page content and produce on-page SEO scores and fixes. Some reference material broadens into E-E-A-T, technical, bulk, and accessibility checks, but these are SEO-adjacent and disclosed rather than hidden capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Top-level instructions say to hand off deep content-quality and technical audits, while templates and rubrics still include quick scoring for those areas. This is a scope-quality issue, not evidence of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains markdown skill/reference files only, with no executable install hooks, bundled scripts, package manager actions, or obfuscated content.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Allowed tool access is limited to WebFetch. Mentions of optional SEO tools, Search Console, crawlers, and local helpers are consistent with SEO auditing and depend on user-provided or already connected data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill asks before saving results and uses a scoped memory path plus open-loop notes. No background persistence, privilege escalation, credential harvesting, or automatic mutation is present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: The audit template includes content-quality and technical fields that are common in SEO reports, though the template is less careful than the main skill about labeling them as preliminary or handoff-worthy.
[SDI-4] expected: CORE-EEAT and page-level technical checks are explicitly included as quick scans in SKILL.md, with stated deferral for full publish-readiness, crawl, indexing, and Core Web Vitals work.
[SDI-1] expected: Bulk auditing is not hidden; SKILL.md advertises a site-wide/bulk mode and links to the playbook. The workflow samples clusters rather than directing unbounded crawling.
[SDI-1] expected: The bulk playbook’s E-E-A-T examples are broader than a narrow title/meta audit, but they are framed as sampled profile findings and next-step recommendations, not autonomous high-impact action.
[SDI-1] expected: The scoring rubric mixes structural SEO, content signals, and page-level technical checks. This may affect audit precision, but it does not add sensitive authority or unsafe execution.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The WCAG accessibility overlay is outside the declared SEO scope and could over-prioritize legal/accessibility findings in an SEO report, but it is plainly documented and only affects recommendations.
llm.guidance: Install this if you want SEO audit guidance for pages or batches of URLs. Treat E-E-A-T, accessibility, and technical-performance findings as preliminary signals and use dedicated specialist skills for those decisions; only allow memory saves or connected SEO/Search Console data when you intend to share that context.
llm.summary: This is a mostly transparent SEO-audit skill with some broader audit checklist items, but no hidden execution, data theft, or destructive behavior.
